ai.literal: To the dream that came with a message from my lover, what hospitality shall I indeed offer?
ai.translation: What hospitality can I offer to the dream that came to me bearing a message from my beloved?
ai.modern: என் காதலரின் தூதுடன் வந்த கனவுக்கு நான் என்ன விருந்து செய்வேன்?
ai.explanation: The heroine, suffering from the pain of separation, experiences a dream in which her lover appears. She views this dream not just as an illusion, but as an honored guest that has traveled to bring her a precious message of love. Overwhelmed with gratitude, she wonders what fitting hospitality or feast (vīrundu) she can offer to welcome this dream. This highlights her deep longing and how even a fleeting dream of her lover is treated as a life-giving blessing.

words.gloss: to the one who united with me

ai.literal: If my fish-like, kohl-smeared eyes, when I beg them, would sleep, I would tell the reality of my survival to the one who united with me in my dreams, alas.
ai.translation: If only my fish-like, kohl-painted eyes would sleep when I beg them to, I could tell my lover, who unites with me in my dreams, the painful reality of how I survive this separation.
ai.modern: மீன் போன்ற மை தீட்டிய என் கண்கள் நான் கெஞ்சி கேட்கும்போது தூங்குமானால், என் கனவில் வந்து என்னோடு கலந்த காதலருக்கு நான் உயிர் பிழைத்திருக்கும் உண்மையைச் சொல்வேன்; ஆனால் அவை தூங்குவதில்லையே!
ai.explanation: The heroine is suffering from the intense pain of separation and can only meet her lover in her dreams. However, her beautiful, fish-like eyes (கயலுண்கண்) refuse to close and sleep, even when she begs them (யான் இரப்ப) to do so. She laments that if they would only sleep (துஞ்சின்), she could see her lover in her dreams and tell him (சாற்றுவேன்) the painful truth of how she barely manages to survive (உயல் உண்மை) without him. The particle 'மன்' at the end emphasizes her regret, indicating that her eyes remain stubbornly awake, denying her even the solace of a dream.

words.gloss: him who does not show love

ai.literal: By waking state him who does not show love, by dream because of seeing, exists my life.
ai.translation: Because I behold him in my dreams who does not show me love in my waking hours, my life still survives.
ai.modern: விழித்திருக்கும்போது எனக்கு அன்பு செய்யாதவரை, கனவில் காண்பதனால் தான் என் உயிர் இன்னும் நிலைத்திருக்கிறது.
ai.explanation: The heroine, suffering from the separation of her lover, explains how she manages to stay alive. While awake, her lover does not come to show her affection or comfort her. However, she is able to see him and experience his love in her dreams. It is this dream-encounter that sustains her spirit and keeps her alive despite the painful reality of her waking hours.

ai.literal: Through dream arises love, in the waking state him who does not show love, seeking, to bring.
ai.translation: My love is sustained only through dreams, which seek out and bring back the beloved who does not show grace in waking reality.
ai.modern: நனவு நிலையில் அன்பு செய்யாத காதலரைத் தேடிக் கொண்டுவந்து தருவதால், கனவின் மூலமாகவே காதல் நிலைபெற்று உண்டாகிறது.
ai.explanation: The heroine explains why she cherishes her dreams. In her waking life, her lover is absent and does not bestow his grace upon her. However, when she sleeps, her dreams actively seek out her distant lover and bring him to her. Therefore, it is only through the medium of dreams that her love is kept alive and nourished.

parts.gloss: that which was seen also (with poetic elongation)

ai.literal: That which was seen in the waking state also at that very moment, a dream indeed is sweet only at the moment it is seen.
ai.translation: Just as what is experienced in the waking state is pleasant only at that very moment, a dream too is pleasant only at the moment it is dreamt.
ai.modern: நனவில் கண்டதும் அந்த நேரத்திலேயே இனிமையானது; அதுபோலக் கனவும் அது காணப்படுகின்ற பொழுதே இனிமையானதாகும்.
ai.explanation: The heroine compares her waking experiences with her dreams. She observes that both waking reality and dreams are fleeting, bringing joy only at the exact moment they are experienced. Once the moment passes, waking pleasures fade into memory, and dreams vanish upon waking. Therefore, she finds solace in her dreams of her lover, as they offer immediate sweetness just like real-life encounters do while they last.

ai.literal: If a thing called waking state does not exist, through dream the beloved would not depart, indeed.
ai.translation: If there were no such thing as the waking state, my beloved would never depart from me, even in dreams.
ai.modern: விழிப்பு நிலை என்று ஒன்று இல்லாதிருந்தால், கனவின் வழியாக என் காதலர் என்னை விட்டு நீங்கவே மாட்டார்.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the heroine expresses her deep longing for her absent lover, whom she can only meet in her dreams. She laments that the waking state (நனவு) is what breaks this beautiful union. If the waking state did not exist at all, she would remain in a continuous dream where her beloved (காதலர்) would never have to depart (நீங்கலர்) from her. The particle 'மன்' emphasizes her sorrow and the painful contrast between the comfort of her dreams and the harsh reality of waking up.

ai.literal: In the waking state, not granting grace, the cruel one, through a dream, why me tormenting?
ai.translation: Why does that cruel man, who does not grant me his grace in my waking hours, still come to torment me in my dreams?
ai.modern: நனவில் அன்பு காட்டாத கொடியவர், கனவின் வழியாக என்னை ஏன் துன்புறுத்துகிறார்?
ai.explanation: The heroine, separated from her lover, laments her painful state. She calls him 'cruel' because he does not show her any grace or return to her during her waking hours. Yet, he constantly appears in her dreams, which only serves to torment her by reminding her of his absence when she wakes up. She questions the fairness of him afflicting her mind through dreams when he refuses to comfort her in reality.

ai.literal: When sleeping, shoulders-upon-he becoming, when waking, heart-of-he he becomes quickly.
ai.translation: When I sleep, he is upon my shoulders; but when I wake up, he quickly becomes the dweller of my heart.
ai.modern: நான் தூங்கும்போது என் தோள்களின் மேல் இருப்பவர், நான் விழிக்கும்போது விரைவாக என் நெஞ்சத்திற்குள் வந்துவிடுகிறார்.
ai.explanation: The heroine describes how her lover never leaves her, transitioning seamlessly between her dreams and her waking thoughts. When she falls asleep, she dreams of him embracing her, making him the one who rests upon her shoulders. The moment she wakes up, he does not vanish into nothingness; instead, he swiftly retreats into her heart as a vivid memory. The word 'நெஞ்சத்தர்' (he of the heart) highlights how his physical absence in the waking world is instantly compensated by his intense presence in her mind.

words.gloss: those who do not bestow love

ai.literal: In the waking state, those who do not bestow love, they will blame; in dream, their lover, those who do not see.
ai.translation: Only those who do not see their lover in their dreams will blame him for not showing love in the waking state.
ai.modern: கனவில் தன் காதலரைக் காணப் பெறாதவர்களே, நனவில் தமக்கு அன்பு செய்யாத காதலரை நொந்து கொள்வார்கள்.
ai.explanation: The heroine explains that she has no reason to complain about her lover's absence or lack of affection during the day. She asserts that only women who are unable to meet their lovers in their dreams (கனவினால் காதலர்க் காணாதவர்) will feel pained and blame them (நோவர்) for not showing love in the waking state (நனவினால் நல்காரை). Since her lover constantly visits and unites with her in her dreams, she remains content and free from resentment.

ai.literal: In the waking state, our (beloved) abandoned (us), they say; in dream, do they not see (him), the people of this town?
ai.translation: The people of this town say that my beloved has abandoned me, judging only by the waking state. Do they not see him coming to me in their own dreams?
ai.modern: விழித்திருக்கும்போது நம் காதலர் நம்மை விட்டுப் பிரிந்துவிட்டார் என்று இவ்வூரார் சொல்கிறார்கள்; அவர்கள் தங்கள் கனவில் அவரைக் காண்பதில்லையோ?
ai.explanation: The heroine is pining for her departed lover, and the townspeople gossip that he has abandoned her. She counters this by stating that he only appears to have left during the waking state (நனவினால்). In her dreams (கனவினால்), he is constantly present with her. She wonders aloud if the townspeople ever experience dreams themselves, as they seem completely ignorant of the nightly reunions she enjoys with her beloved.
